title: High on Rebellion: Inside the Underground at Max's Kansas City

subject_headings: New York (N.Y.) -- Social life and customs

description.main: An account of Max's Kansas City, the New York underground club, with a foreword by Lou Reed.
description.extended:
An account of Max's Kansas City, the New York club and restaurant, by Yvonne Sewall-Ruskin, with a foreword by Lou Reed.

Published in 1998, the book runs to 287 pages plus a front section of xxii. Library subject headings place it under bohemianism, celebrities, restaurants and New York social life and customs. The club it covers opened in 1965 at 213 Park Avenue South and was a meeting point for artists, poets, musicians and Warhol's circle until the original site closed in 1981.

The author is identified in Wikipedia as the partner of Mickey Ruskin, who opened the club. In 2001 she founded the Max's Kansas City Project, a nonprofit that gives emergency funding to people in the arts in crisis.
